h1: The 8 Best Color E-Readers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight color E Ink e-readers from PocketBook, Bigme and Musnap, compared on storage, Android support and size.
summary: The PocketBook Verse Pro Color is the best color e-reader for most people, with a Kaleido 3 screen, IPX8 waterproofing and text-to-speech. Musnap's Neo 2C and Ocean C suit large libraries, comics and notes. The Bigme B6 variants cover cellular data, translation and tight budgets. Pick by software and size first, not by color alone.
intro: Color E Ink looks tempting, but the screen is only half the purchase. The software wrapped around it decides whether the device feels like a simple book or a small, slow tablet. Many readers here run full Android, which opens up apps and flexibility, though it also means more setup than a plain e-book device ever asks of you.

We reviewed eight color e-readers from PocketBook, Musnap and Bigme and ranked them on screen type, storage, Android support, waterproofing and price tier. Everything comes from the spec sheets. We make no claims about screen sharpness or battery life, because the listings give us no data on either.

products.name: PocketBook Verse Pro Color, 6" E Ink Kaleido 3 Display, IPX8 Waterproof
products.verdict: A waterproof, compact reader with a Kaleido 3 color screen.
products.description:
The PocketBook Verse Pro Color has a 6 inch E Ink Kaleido 3 display with IPX8 waterproofing, text-to-speech and Bluetooth audio, in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It leads because it combines a recognized color screen with features the Android devices below do not list. Waterproofing lets it live near a pool or bath, and built-in speech and Bluetooth turn it into an audiobook player. The Musnap models carry more storage and apps, but they are also pricier and more complicated to use.

Buy it if you want a durable, simple reader that does one job well. The caveat is limited app choice, so skip it if you want to install reading services of your own. The screen is also small at 6 inches, which is tight for comics and PDFs.
products.idealFor: Readers who want a durable, simple device.

products.name: Musnap Neo 2C 64GB+4GB Colour eBook Reader, 6" Color E Ink
products.verdict: The newer-generation Musnap with 64GB and 4GB RAM.
products.description:
The Musnap Neo 2C is a 6 inch color E Ink reader with 64GB of storage, 4GB of RAM and third-party app support, in the $200 to $500 bucket. It is the newer generation of the Neo line.

It ranks second because it offers the room and flexibility the PocketBook lacks, and it is newer than the Neo C below with matching memory and storage. What holds it under the Verse Pro Color is price, since it costs more, and it does not list waterproofing.

Buy it if you carry a large library or want to install your own reading apps. Skip it if cost matters most, as the PocketBook and the Bigme models give you color reading for less. The 6 inch screen is also compact, so comics fit better on the Ocean C.

products.name: Musnap Ocean C 64GB+4GB 7" Color eBook Reader, Supports Handwriting
products.verdict: A 7-inch color screen with handwriting support.
products.description:
The Musnap Ocean C is a 7 inch color E Ink reader with handwriting support, 64GB of storage and 4GB of RAM, in the $200 to $500 bucket. It has the largest color screen in the ranking.

It sits third because the Neo 2C is newer and more pocketable, and size is the only thing the Ocean C changes. But for comics, PDFs and note taking, that extra inch is a real advantage that no 6 inch model can match. Handwriting input makes it useful for annotation as well.

Buy it if you read graphic content, documents or want to jot notes on the page. Skip it if you want a reader that slips into a coat pocket, since the larger body is less portable. As with the other Musnaps, the price tier is high.

products.name: Musnap Neo C 64GB+4GB Colour eBook Reader, 6" Color E Ink
products.verdict: Ample storage and RAM in a 6-inch color reader.
products.description:
The Musnap Neo C is a 6 inch color E Ink reader with 64GB of storage, 4GB of RAM and third-party app support, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Fourth place follows from the Neo 2C offering the same memory and storage in a newer generation. That makes the Neo C the choice only if you find it discounted. It stays ahead of the Bigme models because it lists more RAM and a larger storage pool than the cheaper B6 variants, which helps with apps.

Buy it if you want the Musnap hardware class and can find it for less than the 2C. Skip it if you want the latest design. The caveat is that the listing does not separate it from its newer sibling on any spec, so the age of the model is the only difference you can verify.

products.name: Bigme B6 Color eReader, 6" Android E-Ink, 4G+64GB
products.verdict: Android color reading with 4G data and 64GB.
products.description:
The Bigme B6 with 4G is a 6 inch color E Ink reader running Android 14 with 64GB of storage, in the $100 to $200 bucket. It is the only reader here with named 4G connectivity.

It ranks fifth because the Musnap models list more RAM and larger or newer hardware, but nothing else offers cellular data. That is useful if you want to download books on a commute or while traveling away from Wi-Fi. Against the other Bigme models below, the 64GB of storage is double the capacity.

Buy it if you want to sync and download without hunting for a network. The caveat is that cellular data needs a plan, which adds a recurring cost. Skip it if you only read at home on Wi-Fi, since you would pay for a feature you never use.
products.idealFor: Readers wanting data on the go.

products.name: Bigme B6 Color E-Reader, Android 14, Translator & Voice Recorder
products.verdict: Adds a translator and voice recorder to color reading.
products.description:
This Bigme B6 variant runs Android 14 on a color E Ink screen and adds a built-in translator and a voice recorder. It falls in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It ranks sixth because the extras serve a narrow audience. A translator is helpful for language learners reading foreign texts, and a recorder is handy for notes or lectures, but most buyers want a reader first. The 4G model above has broader appeal, and the listing does not state storage, which makes it harder to judge against the others.

Buy it if you study languages or want a single device for reading and voice memos. Skip it if you want a pure reader, because the niche features will not matter. Check the storage size on the page before ordering, since the listing leaves it out.

products.name: Bigme B6 Color eReader, Octa-Core CPU, 2GB+32GB, Android 14
products.verdict: An octa-core budget B6 with 2GB RAM and 32GB.
products.description:
This Bigme B6 lists an octa-core CPU, 2GB of RAM and 32GB of storage, running Android 14 with color E Ink, in the $100 to $200 bucket. The listing highlights it as one of the lowest-priced models.

It ranks seventh because its storage and memory fall behind the 64GB models above. Thirty-two gigabytes is still plenty for a few thousand books, but comics and PDFs can fill it quickly, and apps compete for the same space. The named octa-core processor does give it a clearer performance claim than the plainest Bigme below.

Buy it if you want color reading on a tight budget. Skip it if you store large libraries or want to run several apps at once. In that case, the Bigme with 64GB or a Musnap would be a more comfortable choice.

products.name: Bigme B6 Color Ebook Reader, 2GB+32GB Storage, Android 14, Black
products.verdict: Core Bigme color reading without extras.
products.description:
This Bigme B6 pairs color E Ink with Android 14, 2GB of RAM and 32GB of storage, in black, in the $100 to $200 bucket. It lists no extras beyond the basics.

It finishes last because it adds nothing over the octa-core variant above, which names its processor. The tradeoff is simplicity, since there are no translator, recorder or cellular features to learn. As the plainest Bigme in the group, it makes sense only if its price is better than the alternatives at checkout.

Buy it if you want core color reading and nothing else. Skip it if you want extras or more storage, because both the 64GB Bigme and the Musnap models do more. Thirty-two gigabytes will limit anyone who plans to keep comics and many installed apps on one device.

whatMatters.detail: Screen type describes the display technology. Color E Ink, such as the Kaleido 3 panel on the PocketBook, shows color without the backlit look of an LCD tablet, which many people find easier on the eyes. Check the display name in the listing title, and confirm the screen is color, not black and white.

Storage holds your books, comics and installed apps. A few thousand text books need little, while comics and PDFs fill space quickly. The Musnap models list 64GB and the cheapest Bigme variants list 32GB. Look for the gigabyte figure in the title or specs.

The operating system decides which apps you can install. Android, such as Android 14 on the Bigme B6, lets you add reading services beyond the built-in store, while the PocketBook uses a simpler reader system. Check the Android version, and whether the listing mentions third-party app support, before you buy.

Water resistance is the IPX rating, and IPX8 means the device can handle submersion. It matters if you read in the bath, by a pool or on a beach. Only the PocketBook Verse Pro Color lists it here. Look for the IPX code in the title or bullets.

Screen size changes how you read. A 6 inch reader slips into a pocket, while a 7 inch screen like the Musnap Ocean C gives comics and PDFs more room. Check the size in the title, and think about whether you will mostly read prose or page layouts.

faq.q: Are color e-readers harder on batteries?
faq.a: The listings give no battery data, so we cannot compare them. Color screens and Android software can use more power than a plain reader like the PocketBook, so check the battery details on each page before buying.
Assuming color E Ink looks like a tablet. It does not. Colors are softer than on an LCD, so a reader like the PocketBook Verse Pro Color is best judged as a book with color touches, not a tiny iPad.

Yes, if you want to install reading apps or use features like 4G on the Bigme B6. If you prefer a simple, waterproof device, the PocketBook is easier. The Musnap Neo 2C is better for large libraries and apps.

Depending on the model, you use built-in Wi-Fi apps or transfer files from a computer. Android models like the Bigme B6 can install reading apps, while the PocketBook relies on its own system and file transfer.

faq.q: How do I care for it?
faq.a: Keep the device out of extreme heat and clean it with a dry cloth. Even the PocketBook, rated IPX8, should be dried after use. A cover protects the screen of the Musnap Ocean C in a bag.

faq.q: Can I use it in the bath?
faq.a: Only the PocketBook Verse Pro Color lists IPX8 waterproofing, so it is the one built for bath or poolside reading. The Musnap and Bigme models do not state a water rating, so keep them dry.

finalTake: The PocketBook Verse Pro Color is the best color e-reader for most people, thanks to its waterproof body and simple design. Musnap's Neo 2C and Ocean C are worth the extra money for large libraries, apps and comics. The Bigme B6 variants fill in cellular, translation and budget needs. Choose the software and size you want first.
